ruleset.name: RTP regex hygiene (advisory)
ruleset.description:
Advisory detectors for avoidable regex use: per-call Pattern compilation, String regex helpers on literal input, regex-path String#split, and regex text concatenated without Pattern.quote (injection / wrong-match risk).
Report-only: run by the `pmdRegexMain` task with ignoreFailures = true, so findings are listed but never fail the build. Reports land in `build/reports/pmd/regexMain.{xml,html}` per module and are imported into SonarCloud as external PMD issues (sonar.java.pmd.reportPaths).
.\gradlew.bat pmdRegexMain -PregexAnalysis (all modules) .\gradlew.bat :rtp-core:pmdRegexMain -PregexAnalysis (one module)
`-PstaticAnalysis` also runs this scan (still advisory). Production sources only; tests are not scanned.
Suppress a justified site (e.g. a user-supplied pattern that must compile at runtime) with @SuppressWarnings("PMD.RuleName") plus a short reason.
Not flagged on purpose: static final Pattern fields and static initializers (compiled once), and String#split on a single literal char or an escaped non-alphanumeric char (the JDK fast path never touches java.util.regex).

rule.name: UseStringReplaceForLiteralRegex
rule.message: replaceAll with a literal regex: use String.replace (no Pattern compile, no regex semantics).

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidStringRegexHelpers
rule.message: String.replaceAll/replaceFirst/matches compiles a new Pattern on every call: use a static final Pattern or a char scan.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: AvoidRegexSplit
rule.message: String.split argument misses the JDK single-char fast path and compiles a Pattern per call: use a static final Pattern or a char split.

property.name: xpath

rule.example: s.split(":"); // not flagged (fast path) s.split("\\."); // not flagged (fast path) s.split("\\s+"); // flagged WS.split(s); // preferred: private static final Pattern WS = Pattern.compile("\\s+");

rule.name: RegexCompiledPerCall
rule.message: Pattern compiled per call: hoist to a static final Pattern (suppress with a reason if the pattern is runtime-supplied).

rule.name: UnquotedRegexConcatenation
rule.message: Regex built by concatenating non-constant text without Pattern.quote: quote the dynamic part or avoid regex.

property.name: xpath
property.value: //MethodCall[pmd-java:matchesSig('java.util.regex.Pattern#compile(java.lang.String)') or pmd-java:matchesSig('java.util.regex.Pattern#compile(java.lang.String,int)') or pmd-java:matchesSig('java.util.regex.Pattern#matches(java.lang.String,java.lang.CharSequence)') or pmd-java:matchesSig('java.lang.String#replaceAll(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)') or pmd-java:matchesSig('java.lang.String#replaceFirst(java.lang.String,java.lang.String)') or pmd-java:matchesSig('java.lang.String#matches(java.lang.String)') or pmd-java:matchesSig('java.lang.String#split(java.lang.String)') or pmd-java:matchesSig('java.lang.String#split(java.lang.String,int)')] [ArgumentList/*[1][self::InfixExpression] [not(@CompileTimeConstant = true())] [not(.//MethodCall[pmd-java:matchesSig('java.util.regex.Pattern#quote(java.lang.String)')])]]

rule.example: Pattern.compile("\\[" + key + "]", Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE); // flagged Pattern.compile("\\[" + Pattern.quote(key) + "]", Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE); // compliant
